McLaren.summary: McLaren’s new rear‑wing setting shifts the flap to a “straight‑line” mode, shaving drag off the car so it can hit higher top speeds on the long straights. At the same time, a reshaped floor‑piece smooths the airflow under the car, giving a steadier grip in fast corners. Together they should boost McLaren’s straight‑line punch while keeping the car stable where it matters most for this weekend’s high‑speed circuit.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has stripped off several small winglets from the rear wing and trimmed the rear-view mirrors on the front of the car to lower drag for this circuit’s high‑speed layout. The cleaner aero package should give the team a bit more straight‑line speed and better tyre preservation, helping them stay competitive in qualifying and the race. In short, less “fuss” on the car means more pace where it counts this weekend.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has tweaked a handful of parts to make the RB‑19 both tougher and a bit more aero‑efficient for the upcoming Grand Prix – the rear‑suspension‑to‑wheel link has been strengthened to curb any reliability hiccups, while a new floor edge shape and a revised exhaust‑tailpipe bracket also boost durability and keep the car’s balance steady. A subtle reshaping of the front‑wing endplate vanes fine‑tunes the airflow into the car, giving Max a little extra grip out of the corners. Together these updates aim to keep the car on the limit longer and avoid any surprise failures during the weekend.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari’s weekend update trims drag all over the car – the front floor now has a single, slimmer element, the side‑mirror support is shorter and tucked into the sidepod, the rear‑brake‑duct winglet has been stripped away, and the rear‑wing tail now carries a narrow central slot with slimmer side flaps. All of these tweaks clean up the airflow, giving the car a bit more straight‑line speed and steadier handling on the high‑speed sections of the circuit, which could make a real difference in qualifying and the race.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams has added a narrow vertical fence around the Halo for this circuit, aiming to clean up airflow and give the car a bit more straight‑line stability. The front wing’s end‑plates have been narrowed, which should smooth out the front balance and make the car easier to drive through the corners. Finally, a small tweak to the floor’s underside trims down drag, helping the car hit higher speeds on the straights without sacrificing too much downforce. All three changes are about getting a tighter, more predictable feel and a little extra top‑end speed for this weekend’s track.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls has fitted a new rear‑wing assembly with a revised drag‑range mechanism, letting the car dial down drag or boost down‑force more precisely for the track’s demands. They’ve also moved the exhaust tailpipe and reshaped its bracket, smoothing the airflow off the back of the car. Together these tweaks give the RB a tighter aero balance and a little extra straight‑line speed, which could be the edge they need on the weekend’s high‑speed sections.

Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has tweaked two key aero bits for this weekend: the front‑suspension fairings have been reshaped, and the edge of the floor just ahead of the rear tyre has been refined. The new fairings clean up the airflow over the front, giving the car a steadier front end, while the floor‑edge tweak smooths the low‑pressure tunnel under the car for extra rear‑wheel grip. Together they should translate into more consistent cornering speed and a stronger push off the straights when the laps count.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has given the car a fresh look for the weekend, starting with a revamped front floor and diffuser that should tighten the airflow under the car and boost straight‑line grip. The sidepods and engine cover have been slimmed down, helping the car cut cleaner through the corners, while a reshaped rear‑suspension fairing and new drum deflectors aim to keep the rear more stable under heavy braking. Together, these tweaks are meant to improve overall balance and give the team a bit more pace on both the straights and the twisty sections of the circuit.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has reshaped the front‑wing endplate’s foot‑vane to boost bite in the corners, giving the car a steadier feel when it’s on the limit. They also stripped off the SM‑pod fairing on the rear wing, trimming unnecessary drag so the car can hit a higher top‑end on the straights. Together, these tweaks aim to make the car both more confident through twisty sections and quicker on the long laps of this weekend’s circuit.

Cadillac.summary: Cadillac’s latest tweaks move the front‑floor support a bit farther out and higher, tightening the airflow under the car, while a new small wing‑like piece on the outer diffuser edge smooths the slipstream at the rear. Together they give the car a boost in grip and stability, meaning the drivers can carry more speed through the corners and stay glued to the track this weekend.
